nota: Unofficial translation of the syllabus of the Spanish competitive examination for entry into the High Corps of Spanish State Economists and Trade Experts (TCEE). The official titles are the Spanish ones in temario.json.

temas.titulo: Subject matter and methods of economic science. Current issues and debates, with special reference to behavioral economics.
The classical economists and Marx.
The neoclassical economists.
Keynes's economic thought. Reference to post-Keynesian economics and disequilibrium.
The neoclassical synthesis. Monetarism.
The new classical macroeconomics. The rational expectations hypothesis; the Lucas critique; the emergence of dynamic stochastic general equilibrium models.
New Keynesian economics. First and second generations.
Consumer demand theory (I). Axioms on preferences, utility function, and Marshallian demand function. Revealed preference theory. Hedonic prices.
Consumer demand theory (II). Duality and integrability of preferences. Demand systems used in empirical studies. Measures of welfare change.
Consumer demand theory (III). Consumer choice under risk and uncertainty.

Production theory. Characterization of the firm's technology in the short and long run. The production possibility set. The production function. Local and global returns to scale. Elasticity of substitution. Joint production.
Cost theory. Duality analysis in the theory of the firm. Empirical applications.
Economics of information and agency theory: adverse selection and moral hazard.
Game theory. Main concepts. Applications, with special reference to auctions.
The firm: efficient size and its limits. Special mention of transaction cost economics. Industrial organization theory: barriers to entry and contestable markets.
Market analysis (I). The perfect competition model. Partial equilibrium analysis: short and long run; adjustment dynamics and stability of equilibrium. Efficiency and welfare analysis.
Market analysis (II). Monopoly theory. Price discrimination. Natural monopoly. Joint production. Efficiency and welfare analysis. Monopsony. Bilateral monopoly.
Market analysis (III). Product differentiation: the theory of monopolistic competition and other developments.
Market analysis (IV). Oligopoly theory: noncooperative and cooperative solutions.
Market power and optimal regulation. Definition of the relevant market. Developments under asymmetric information. Practical applications.
General equilibrium theory.
Welfare economics (I). The fundamental theorems of welfare economics. Economic optimum and the second best.
Welfare economics (II). Market failures: externalities and public goods. Intervention and government failures.
Welfare economics (III). Social welfare functions. Collective choice theory. Arrow's impossibility theorem and subsequent developments.
The neoclassical theory of the labor market. Intertemporal analysis of labor supply. Human capital theory. The human capital earnings function and empirical evidence.
Frictional unemployment. The Beveridge curve, the Diamond-Mortensen-Pissarides search and matching model. Adjustment costs and labor demand dynamics.
Wage determination: bargaining models, efficiency wages, and implicit contracts.
The natural rate of unemployment and the NAIRU. The persistence of unemployment.
Dynamic modeling of decision-making. Infinite-horizon models and overlapping generations models.
Macroeconomic aggregates and national accounts.
Analysis of input-output tables.
The aggregate supply and demand model: determination of income and inflation in an open economy. Analysis of monetary and fiscal policies, and of supply shocks and supply-side policies.
Theories of current consumption demand: life cycle and permanent income. The demand for consumer durables. Empirical evidence and economic policy implications.
Theories of investment in capital goods. Uncertainty and irreversibility of investment. Economic policy implications.
Theories of money demand. Economic policy implications.
Monetary policy (I). The design and implementation of monetary policy.

Monetary policy (II). The transmission mechanisms of conventional monetary policy. Price rigidities, wage rigidities, and financial frictions. The transmission mechanisms of unconventional monetary policy.
Fiscal policy: effects on economic growth and saving.
Public deficit. Concepts. Financing and its macroeconomic consequences. Monetary dominance and fiscal dominance. Public debt dynamics and sustainability.
Effectiveness and interaction of monetary and fiscal policies in the main developed economies since the Great Recession of 2008. The size of fiscal multipliers.
Inflation: causes and effects on economic efficiency and welfare. Hyperinflation and deflation.
Business cycle theories: nominal and real cycles. Reference to the financial cycle and its interactions with the real cycle.
Economic growth (I). Capital accumulation and exogenous technical progress. The Solow model. The Solow model augmented with human capital accumulation. The Ramsey-Cass-Koopmans model.
Economic growth (II). Endogenous growth models: increasing returns, human capital, and technological innovation.

Empirical evidence on economic growth and on the distribution of income among factors of production. Growth accounting, with special reference to total factor productivity. International economic convergence.

partes.nombre: Financial economics, international economics, and international economic relations

temas.titulo: Financial reporting of firms: statements of financial position and flow statements. Methods of economic and financial analysis of the firm.
The firm and investment decisions. Alternative project appraisal criteria. Return, risk, and cost of capital.
The firm and financing decisions: equity versus debt financing. Dividend policy and capital structure.
Analysis of the growth of the firm. Firm valuation methods. Special reference to mergers, acquisitions, and strategic alliances.

International trade theory (I). The Ricardian theory of comparative advantage. Determination of the terms of trade. The specific factors model. The Heckscher-Ohlin-Samuelson (H-O-S) model; theorems derived from the model and extensions.
International trade theory (II). New trade theory. Special reference to imperfect competition, increasing returns, and firm heterogeneity.
Trade policy (I). Instruments and effects. Tariff and nontariff barriers. Other traditional instruments.
Trade policy (II). Strategic trade policy.
International trade and economic growth. Special reference to the effects of trade on growth.
Theory of economic integration.
The balance of payments: concept, measurement, and interpretation.
Balance-of-payments adjustment mechanisms. Special reference to the intertemporal approach to the balance of payments. Analysis of the sustainability of the deficit and of external debt.
Foreign exchange markets: transactions and instruments.
Theories of exchange rate determination.
Comparative analysis of exchange rate regimes. Intervention in and regulation of foreign exchange markets.
Theory of monetary integration.
Theories explaining balance-of-payments crises.

The new economic and financial globalization. Determinants and effects of international factor movements: labor mobility, portfolio investment, and direct investment, with special reference to global value chains.
International coordination of economic policies. Theoretical and practical aspects. The G20, the OECD, and other international forums.
The international economic system from the 19th century to the breakdown of the Bretton Woods system.
The international economic system since the end of the Bretton Woods system.
The International Monetary Fund. Structure and policies. Crisis prevention and resolution.
Analysis of equity instruments. Fundamental analysis. Portfolio choice theory. The capital asset pricing model (CAPM). Arbitrage pricing theory (APT). Technical analysis.
Analysis of fixed-income instruments. Determination of bond prices and yields. The term structure of interest rates. Assessment of bond risk and return: duration and convexity.
Analysis of derivative instruments and markets.
Financial crises and bank runs; special reference to the international financial crisis that began in 2007–2008. Risk management in financial institutions.
Bank and nonbank financial regulation. Theoretical foundations and empirical evidence.
Economics of developing countries. Recent theories of economic development. Empirical evidence, with special reference to the experimental approach, and implications for policy design.
External financing of economic development. The external debt problem. Development aid.
The World Bank Group, the regional development banks, and other multilateral development finance institutions.
Climate change and its impact on the economy. Evidence and integrated assessment models. International agreements and main measures adopted to address climate change.
Global economic outlook. Sectoral and geographical structure of international trade and financial flows. The new emerging areas.
The WTO. Background and current organization. The GATT and the agreements on trade in goods. Current situation.
The WTO. Agreements other than those on goods.
Non-EU integration processes.
Treaties, legal order, and institutions of the European Union.
The finances of the European Union and the EU budget. The current multiannual financial framework.
The agricultural policy of the European Union. Economic problems and reform processes. The Common Fisheries Policy.
The single market of the European Union. The principle of free movement of goods, services, persons, and capital. Competition policy.
Economic and social cohesion in the European Union: regional policy and budgetary and financial instruments. Social and employment policy. The process of real convergence in the European Union.
The trade policy of the European Union.
The external economic relations of the European Union. The development cooperation policy of the European Union.

The origin of the euro: functioning and evolution of the European Monetary System. The nominal convergence criteria. The European System of Central Banks: objectives and instruments. Monetary policy in the euro area since 2009.
The Banking Union: pillars and the single rulebook. The Capital Markets Union.

Economic governance of the European Union and the euro area. The European Semester. Fiscal rules and the Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure. The European Stability Mechanism. The common fiscal policy response since COVID-19.
Spanish statistical sources. Methodologies and limitations.
Human resources in Spain: demographic structure and human capital. Medium- and long-term population projections: implications for economic growth.
The personal and factor distribution of income in Spain. Inequality of income, wealth, and consumption. The redistributive effect of the Spanish public sector.
The agriculture and fisheries sectors in Spain.
Structure of the energy sector and its subsectors: electricity system, gas system, and petroleum products. New technologies and challenges for the sector.
Spanish energy and climate policy: climate change mitigation and adaptation. Relationship with EU energy and climate policy. Sectoral environmental policies.

The science and technology system and policy in Spain. Relationship with the European Union's R&D policy. Research, development, and innovation (R&D&I) activity in the public and private sectors. Comparison with international good practice.

The firm in Spain. Main characteristics: productivity, internationalization, size, and financing. Comparison between industrial firms and service firms. The business climate in Spain. The public enterprise sector.
Analysis of industry in Spain. Characteristics and current situation. The challenges of industry and industrial policy in Spain in the context of developed economies. The EU strategy.

Sectoral structure of industry in Spain. Classification of sectors by level of technological content and of demand. Analysis of the main sectors: the agri-food industry, the automotive industry, the chemical and pharmaceutical industry, and capital goods and high-technology manufacturing.
The construction sector in Spain. The housing market. Housing and land: problems and policy.
Structure and policy of the transportation and telecommunications sectors in Spain.
Tourism in Spain: trends, challenges, and tourism policy.
Structure, policies, and challenges of the distribution sector (wholesale and retail trade), with special reference to e-commerce.
Competition enforcement and advocacy in Spain. Principles of efficient economic regulation. Guarantee of market unity.
The labor market in Spain. Characteristics, functioning, and problems. Employment policies.
The economy of the Spanish regions: regional specialization, real convergence, and regional development policy.

The Spanish financial system (I). Recent developments in the financial system. Genesis and development of the crisis of the Spanish financial system that began in 2008. The restructuring of credit institutions. The Financial Assistance Programme.
The Spanish financial system (II). Credit institutions in Spain: current structure of the Spanish banking sector and main indicators. The regulatory, supervisory, and crisis management framework.
The Spanish financial system (III). Securities markets and other forms of nonbank financing: agents and instruments. Financial innovation.

Analysis of trends in Spain's balance of payments and international investment position since the adoption of the euro. Net position of the Banco de España vis-à-vis the Eurosystem. External sustainability.

The internationalization of the Spanish economy (I). Current sectoral and geographical structure of Spain's goods and services account. Competitiveness indicators. Spain's integration into global value chains.
The internationalization of the Spanish economy (II). Current sectoral and geographical structure of foreign investment in Spain and of Spanish investment abroad.
Spanish internationalization policy (I). Financial instruments to support exports and investment abroad. Evaluation and comparison with international good practice.
Spanish internationalization policy (II). Trade promotion. Bodies and instruments. Evaluation and comparison with international good practice.
Development cooperation policy in Spain. Technical and financial cooperation instruments. Evaluation of policy design and economic impact analysis.

The Spanish economy in the period 1959–1999. The 1959 Stabilization Plan. The Spanish economy in the 1960s. The energy crises of the 1970s. Accession to the European Communities. The macroeconomic adjustment process for entry into the euro area.
The evolution of the Spanish economy and economic policy from the creation of the euro area to 2019. Special reference to the economic and financial crisis that began in 2008.

The evolution of the Spanish economy and economic policy since the COVID-19 crisis. Current situation and outlook of the Spanish economy. Spain's macroeconomic imbalances under the EU Macroeconomic Imbalance Procedure.

Spain's financial relations with the European Union: budgetary and off-budget flows, and the Spain–EU net financial balance. Recent trends and current situation. Spain in the 2021–2027 Multiannual Financial Framework. Spain's real convergence with the European Union.
The public sector: delimitation, transactions, and main accounts according to the European System of Accounts.
Public sector decision-making mechanisms. Voting rules. Representative democracy. Public production and bureaucracy. Justification for legal limits on public sector activity.
The budget as an instrument of redistribution. The welfare state: instruments, problems, and reforms. Measurement and indicators of redistributive impact.
The budget as a compensatory (stabilizing) instrument for economic activity. Discretionary and automatic components of the budget: cyclical balance, structural balance, and fiscal effort.
Public expenditure. Reasons for its growth. The debate on the size of government with regard to expenditure. International comparisons.
Public policy evaluation. Impact evaluation techniques. Cost-benefit analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, and other evaluation techniques.
Government revenue. Defining elements and types of taxes. Principles of taxation.
Tax shifting and incidence in competitive and monopolistic markets. Partial and general equilibrium approaches.
Income and substitution effects of taxes. Concept and measurement of excess burden. Measures of tax progressivity.
Taxation and supply. Incentive effects of taxes.
Optimal taxation. The optimal tax rate. The Ramsey rule. The efficiency-equity trade-off in tax policy.
Direct taxation: theory and international comparisons.
Indirect taxation: theory and international comparisons.
The theory of fiscal federalism: the optimal assignment of functions among levels of government to achieve maximum welfare. The financing of subnational governments: taxes, transfers, and debt.
Public enterprise. Reasons for its existence. Privatization policy. International comparisons.
Personal income tax in Spain.
Corporate income tax in Spain.
International taxation. Non-resident income tax in Spain. Double taxation conventions, with special reference to the OECD Model Tax Convention. The problem of base erosion and proposed solutions.
Wealth taxation in Spain: the wealth tax, the inheritance and gift tax, the transfer and stamp duty, and the property tax.
Indirect taxation in Spain: VAT and excise duties.

Legal and institutional framework of budgets in Spain. Budgetary principles, with special reference to stability and sustainability. The General State Budget: preparation, approval, execution, and control. Classifications of revenue and expenditure. Budget amendments.
Key figures of the General State Budget (PGE). Economic, organizational, and spending-policy classifications. Consolidated view of the PGE.

General government finances in Spain in national accounts terms. Current situation and outlook according to the Stability Programme. Revenue structure and tax burden. Expenditure by function according to the COFOG classification. Distribution of public expenditure and revenue by general government subsector.
The Social Security system in Spain. Benefits and their financing. Sustainability of the public pension system.
Regional and local governments in Spain. Powers and financing systems. Regional and local government debt.
The budget balance and debt of general government in Spain: analysis of recent trends and international comparison. Current Treasury funding policy.
